 Taylor Swift is performing at the 60th Annual CMA Awards in Nashville, Tennessee, the Country Music Association announced Friday.
 Swift will perform on Wednesday, Nov. 18 at Bridgestone Arena, which will be her first CMA Awards performance in 13 years. Swift announced she'd be attending the awards ceremony after being nominated for Single of the Year with “I Knew It, I Knew You."
 PREVIOUS COVERAGE | 'I Haven't Yee'd My Last Haw': Taylor Swift attending 60th CMA Awards 
 Her nod for Single of the Year adds to her 25 previous CMA nominations. Swift first came to the CMA Awards in 2006, took home her first award in 2007 and is still the youngest artist to win Entertainer of the Year, which she did in 2009.
 The 60th annual CMA Awards will be hosted by Lainey Wilson for the third year in a row. Performers announced so far for country music's biggest night include Luke Combs, Ella Langley and Chris Stapleton. 
 Attendees can also look forward to special performances celebrating Brooks & Dunn, with Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, Halestorm, HARDY and Marcus King coming together for a tribute in honor of the duo’s Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award. CMA officials also announced a special tribute to Dolly Parton, but the performers for the tribute have yet to be announced.
 Ella Langley and Miranda Lambert top nominations this year with Langley receiving nine nods and Lambert standing out with seven nods. Kacey Musgraves and Ben West each picked up five nominations.
 Organizers have not yet shared the full list of presenters for this year’s show. FOX 17 News will be on the red carpet and inside the awards ceremony, so stick with us for all your CMA Awards coverage.
